_about: Every adjustable BSG business value the engine uses. Each entry is {value, source, provisional}: source = who decided it and where it is written (CLAUDE.md section), provisional = true when Gus said it may change. Change values here, not in the code. Entries with used_from are not read by the code yet; they come in with that step D rule. Lengths in metres unless the key says _mm.

height.source: Standard melamine sheet height (§4). 2.4 m jobs set sheet_h: 2.4 in job.json.

heights.source: Gus, 2026-11-01 (v1.1 §4): melamine comes in only two heights. layout_gen.sheet_for picks the smallest at or above the hoarding height (cut down to it, cut-offs to tops stock), else the tallest + tops (step D rule 6).

spare.source: Gus, 2026-10-21 (§3): always send 2 extra sheets in case of damage on site.

return.source: §2 default return. Used when drafting job.json; the code always reads return from job.json.

door_width.source: §2 default entry width. Used when drafting job.json.

door_height.source: §2 default entry height; used when job.json has no door_height. The grid sheet only dimensions a door height that differs from it (Gus, 2026-10-21).

doors.source: BSG paper form / §3: one double door = 2 leaves.

studs_full_height.source: BSG paper form / §3: door studs 2 x full height.

studs_short.source: BSG paper form / §3: door studs + 4 x 2.3.

studs_short_length.source: BSG paper form / §3. Purpose of the 2.3 m studs still unknown (Gus to ask his boss).

doors.source: Gus, 2026-11-01 (v1.1 §3): one normal door cut in half makes both leaves, so the form lists 1 door.

spare.source: Gus, 2026-11-01 (v1.1 §3): uprights = joints (both run ends included) + 10% spare, rounded up; on external jobs the 10% goes on the joints + 40% total (24 -> 34 -> 38).

matrix.source: BSG weight matrix, Internal Hoardings (Impact Certification Standards), Gus 2026-11-01 (§6): weights per upright by height, first row at or above the hoarding height, no bracing. Weights to send = all uprights incl. the spare uprights x this value; no separate spare weights (Gus, 2026-11-01).

extra_uprights.source: Gus, 2026-11-01, David Jones Lift Area (§7): 40% more uprights on external jobs, rounded up. Not an official table: replace it when Gus sends one. job.json extra_uprights still overrides it for one job.

weights_per_upright.source: Gus, 2026-11-01 (§7): 8 counterweights per upright on external jobs instead of the matrix. Not an official table. job.json weights_per_upright still overrides it for one job.

per_length.source: Run length the factors below are counted per (Just Cuts job, §3).

studs.source: 14 x 70x45 MGP10 studs per 8.8 m, rounded up: inferred from Just Cuts, not formally confirmed (§3).

white_tape.source: 8 rolls of white tape per 8.8 m, rounded up: inferred from Just Cuts (v1). Used while tape.tape_rule is "v1"; the v1.1 joint calculation is behind that switch (step D rule 4).

form_quantities.source: Fixed quantities per job on BSG's paper materials form (Just Cuts example, §3). Rows not listed here stay blank on the form.

roll_length.source: BSG paper form: white tape comes in 25 m rolls; Gus 2026-11-01 (v1.1 §3), confirmed 2026-11-02.

tape_rule.source: Switch for the white tape rolls on the form: "joints" = total joint length / roll_length + spare (v1.1 §3, hoarding/tape.py), switched on by Gus 2026-11-02 (readings A and B: the door sides and top count as written, also on a full-height door); "v1" = materials.white_tape per 8.8 m (Just Cuts), kept to compare.

spare.source: Gus, 2026-11-02: 100% spare (double), rounded up. They always send almost double because changes on site mean removing tape and applying new; tape is cheap. Was 20% (Gus 2026-11-01). Provisional until Gus's boss confirms it (on his list).

roll_length.source: Gus, 2026-11-02: black skirting tape 100 mm comes in 25 m rolls.

spare.source: Gus, 2026-11-02: black tape = full run lineal metres (returns and entry included) x 2 (100% spare, like the white tape) / roll_length, rounded up. Was a fixed 1 roll per job (Just Cuts form).

rounding.source: Gus, 2026-11-01 (§12): money is rounded to the cent, half a cent up (Python decimal rounding mode).

name.value: BSG Commercial Internal Hoarding Schedule of Rates for GPT - Pacific Fair 25-26
name.source: Rate card BSG Hoarding Rate - Pacific Fair 25-26, effective 18/6/2025-30/6/2026; Gus confirmed on 2026-11-01 to keep using it until he sends a new one (§12). Every rate_card value is provisional for that reason.

bands.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): $ per lineal metre ex GST, smallest band at or above the job height. Over 6.0 m = POA.

kiosk.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): 1.2 m kiosk $115/lm, 15 lm minimum.

min_lm.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): 10 lm minimum charge for non-kiosk hoardings.

extra_doors_during.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): extra double doors $400/set during installation.

extra_doors_after.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): extra double doors $800/set after installation.

modification_min.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): post-install modification $800 minimum ($680 for hoardings before 1/10/2025, not used in quotes).

cancel_after_5pm.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): cancellation after 5 pm / dispatched.

included_door_mm.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): 1 set of double doors 2340 x 1600 included.

months_on_site.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): up to 6 months on site included.

scissor_lift_over.source: Rate card 25-26 (§12): scissor lift not included over 4.2 m.

graphics_waste.source: Rate card 25-26 terms: allow 10% waste for graphics.
